ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Policy-gradient label correction on CIFAR-10 with instance-dependent noise
PROPOSAL: A small policy network reads a sample's features from a ResNet-18 and its observed label, then chooses to keep the label or switch to one of the top-3 classes predicted by an exponential-moving-average teacher. The reward is the later drop in teacher loss on a held-out noisy split, so decisions are scored by their lasting effect. We train on CIFAR-10 with instance-dependent noise at 40 percent, generated from a trained network's confusion, and report test accuracy and label precision.
CONTROLS: Cross-entropy on noisy labels; greedy correction by teacher argmax; a policy with no later reward (immediate reward only); DivideMix and ELR+ as reference methods; three seeds with standard deviations.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Expect the policy to beat greedy correction by about two points of test accuracy at 40 percent noise. It may fail if the reward is too noisy for the policy to separate good from bad switches.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reinforcement-learning label correction for CIFAR-10 with a wide search over policy designs
PROPOSAL: A policy network reads features from a ResNet-34 and the observed label, and chooses to keep it or switch to one of the top-5 classes proposed by a teacher; the reward is the drop in teacher loss on a held-out split at five horizons of delay. We train with four policy architectures, six entropy bonuses and three reward shapes on CIFAR-10 with instance-dependent noise at 20, 40 and 60 percent from a trained network's confusion, and report test accuracy and label precision.
CONTROLS: Cross-entropy on noisy labels; greedy correction by teacher argmax; a policy with immediate reward only; DivideMix, ELR+ and UNICON as reference methods; five seeds with standard deviations per design.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Expect the best design to beat greedy correction by about two points at 40 percent noise. It may fail if differences among designs stay within seed variation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploration in label correction: Thompson sampling versus greedy choices on CIFAR-100
PROPOSAL: Each noisy sample keeps a posterior over its candidate true classes, updated from the training-loss trajectory of a ResNet-34. At every round, correction is chosen by Thompson sampling rather than the posterior mode, so uncertain samples are revisited before commitment. On CIFAR-100 with instance-dependent noise at 40 percent we measure how many initially wrong corrections are later recovered, along with final accuracy, against mode-based correction.
CONTROLS: Mode-based correction; confidence-threshold selection with small-loss samples; Co-teaching as a selection reference; SOP as a robust-loss reference; five seeds; recovery rate with bootstrap intervals.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Expect exploration to recover over a quarter of early mistakes and add about one accuracy point. It may fail when 100 classes dilute each posterior, leaving samples with too few visits.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Posterior-sampling and optimism-based correction on CIFAR-100 under four noise rates
PROPOSAL: Every noisy training sample carries a posterior over candidate true classes, refreshed from the loss trajectory of a ResNet-50. Corrections are drawn by Thompson sampling, UCB or epsilon-greedy selection, giving doubtful samples revisits before a label is fixed. On CIFAR-100 with instance-dependent noise at four rates, we count initially wrong corrections that are later reversed, report final accuracy against mode-based correction, and compare four exploration schedules.
CONTROLS: Mode-based correction; confidence-threshold selection with small-loss samples; Co-teaching and DivideMix as selection references; SOP as a robust-loss reference; three seeds; recovery rate with bootstrap intervals.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Expect exploration to recover over a quarter of early mistakes and add about one point of accuracy. It may fail when 100 classes dilute each posterior across the schedules.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Choosing the discount for long-horizon correction rewards
PROPOSAL: The correction policy of a sequential method is trained with discount factors 0, 0.5 and 0.9, where the reward is the change in clean-looking agreement between predictions and corrected labels after a delay of a few epochs. A ResNet-18 learns CIFAR-10 with instance-dependent noise at 30 percent. We plot test accuracy against discount, and track how often a correction that lowered immediate agreement raised later accuracy, using the true labels only for evaluation.
CONTROLS: Immediate-reward policy; no-correction baseline with early stopping; a policy that receives true-label rewards as an oracle ceiling; three seeds; paired differences with intervals.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Expect discount 0.9 to beat discount 0 by one to two points, with the oracle ceiling a further point above. It may fail if the delay is too short to expose long-term effects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Discount, horizon and delay study for correction rewards under instance-dependent noise
PROPOSAL: The correction policy of a sequential method is trained with discount factors from 0 to 0.99, and five delay lengths, where the reward is the change in agreement between predictions and corrected labels. A ResNet-34 learns CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with instance-dependent noise at 30 percent. We plot test accuracy per setting, and track how often a correction that lowered immediate agreement raised later accuracy.
CONTROLS: Immediate-reward policy; no-correction baseline with early stopping; a policy that receives true-label rewards as an oracle ceiling; three seeds; paired differences with intervals for all settings.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Expect discount 0.9 to beat discount 0 by one to two points, with the oracle ceiling a point above. It may fail if the delays are too short or too long to expose long-term effects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Clothing1M evaluation of policy-based label correction
PROPOSAL: We train a ResNet-50 initialized from ImageNet on the Clothing1M training set of 1000000 noisy web images, with a correction policy that explores alternative labels and receives delayed rewards from the teacher's loss on the 50000-image clean-verified split used for validation only. We run 15 epochs with a balanced sample of 64000 images per epoch and report top-1 accuracy on the 10000 clean test images, plus the proportion of labels changed.
CONTROLS: Cross-entropy; DivideMix; ELR+; greedy teacher correction; a policy without exploration; five seeds with ranges.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Expect about 74 percent top-1, above greedy correction by one point. It may fail because Clothing1M noise is partly systematic confusion between similar garments, which exploration cannot undo.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Clothing1M and WebVision evaluation of policy-based label correction with long schedules
PROPOSAL: We train ResNet-50 and Inception-ResNet-v2 networks initialized from ImageNet on the Clothing1M training set of 1000000 noisy web images and on the WebVision training subset of 2400000 images, with a correction policy that explores alternative labels and receives delayed rewards from teacher loss on the clean-verified split. We run 60 epochs and report top-1 accuracy on the 10000 clean test images and on the 50000 WebVision validation images, plus the proportion of labels changed.
CONTROLS: Cross-entropy; DivideMix; ELR+; UNICON; greedy teacher correction; a policy without exploration; five seeds with ranges.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Expect about 74 percent top-1 on Clothing1M, above greedy correction by one point. It may fail because the noise is partly systematic confusion between similar items, which exploration cannot undo.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Human-annotated noise in CIFAR-N: does exploration help beyond synthetic noise?
PROPOSAL: CIFAR-10N worst-case labels (about 40 percent noisy) come from crowd annotators and correlate with image appearance. We train a ResNet-18 with a correction policy that explores alternative labels and receives delayed rewards, and compare against greedy correction. Beyond accuracy we measure how the corrected labels agree with the consensus of annotators, and whether sample difficulty (distance to the decision boundary) predicts policy mistakes.
CONTROLS: Cross-entropy on worst labels; greedy correction; a symmetric-noise-tuned robust loss; the aggregate-label training as ceiling; three seeds; bootstrap intervals.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Expect about 86 percent accuracy, above greedy correction by one point. It may fail if annotator noise is so systematic that no label proposal beats the observed one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Crowd-annotation noise benchmark with exploration, agreement and difficulty analyses at four splits
PROPOSAL: CIFAR-10N worst, aggregate and random labels, and CIFAR-100N fine labels (up to 40 percent noisy) come from crowd annotators and correlate with image appearance. We train ResNet-18, ResNet-34 and PreAct networks with a correction policy that explores alternative labels and receives delayed rewards, and compare against greedy correction. Beyond accuracy we measure agreement of corrected labels with the annotator consensus, and whether difficulty predicts policy mistakes at three depths.
CONTROLS: Cross-entropy on worst labels; greedy correction; a robust loss tuned for symmetric noise; aggregate-label training as ceiling; five seeds; bootstrap intervals per split and each network.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Expect about 86 percent accuracy, above greedy correction by one point. It may fail if annotator noise is so systematic that no label proposal beats the observed one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Extreme noise: CIFAR-10 at 60 and 70 percent instance-dependent corruption
PROPOSAL: At 60 and 70 percent instance-dependent noise the small-loss assumption breaks, since wrong labels become the majority for some classes. We test a correction policy that explores alternatives and learns from delayed rewards, with a teacher warmed up on a class-balanced confident subset. A ResNet-18 trains for 200 epochs, and we report accuracy and the fraction of classes whose labels were majority-corrupted but recovered.
CONTROLS: Small-loss selection with semi-supervised training; greedy correction; the policy without warm-up; ELR+ and CORES2 as references; five seeds; per-class recovery with bootstrap intervals.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Expect the policy to retain above 80 percent accuracy at 60 percent noise while selection falls under 70. It may fail at 70 percent, where the warm-up subset itself becomes unreliable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Extreme noise on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100: many corruption rates, teachers and warm-up lengths
PROPOSAL: At three high instance-dependent noise rates the small-loss assumption breaks, since wrong labels become the majority for some classes. We test a correction policy that explores alternatives and learns from delayed rewards, with teachers of three sizes warmed up on a class-balanced confident subset for five different lengths. ResNet-18 and ResNet-34 networks train for 400 epochs on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and we report accuracy and the fraction of classes recovered.
CONTROLS: Small-loss selection with semi-supervised training; greedy correction; the policy without warm-up; ELR+, CORES2 and DivideMix as references; three seeds; per-class recovery with bootstrap intervals.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Expect the policy to retain above 80 percent accuracy at 60 percent noise on CIFAR-10 while selection falls under 70. It may fail at 80 percent, where the warm-up subset becomes unreliable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Animal-10N and mini WebVision transfer of the correction policy
PROPOSAL: On Animal-10N (50000 training images, roughly 8 percent human-made label noise from similar-looking animals) and on the first 50 classes of WebVision (about 65000 images), we train a ResNet-34 and an Inception-ResNet-v2 with a correction policy that explores alternative labels. We compare final top-1 accuracy and top-5 accuracy, and inspect the corrected confusions between look-alike classes such as cat and lynx for 100 randomly chosen samples.
CONTROLS: Cross-entropy; DivideMix; greedy correction; the policy without exploration; reference numbers rerun with the same augmentation; three seeds.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Expect a gain of 1 to 2 points over greedy correction on both sets. It may fail on Animal-10N, where low noise leaves little to correct.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Animal-10N, full WebVision and ILSVRC transfer of the correction policy with many networks
PROPOSAL: On Animal-10N (50000 training images), the full WebVision set of 2400000 images and 1000 classes, we train a ResNet-50 and an Inception-ResNet-v2 with a correction policy that explores alternative labels, and evaluate on the ILSVRC validation images of 50000. We compare top-1 and top-5 accuracy, and inspect the corrected confusions between look-alike classes such as cat and lynx for 500 randomly chosen samples at 3 training lengths.
CONTROLS: Cross-entropy; DivideMix; UNICON; greedy correction; the policy without exploration; reference numbers rerun with the same augmentation; three seeds.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Expect a gain of 1 to 2 points over greedy correction on both sets. It may fail on Animal-10N, where low noise leaves little to correct.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Combining policy-based correction with semi-supervised training of suspected-noisy samples
PROPOSAL: Samples flagged as noisy by a two-component mixture fit on per-sample losses are treated as unlabeled and receive labels from a correction policy that explores alternatives and learns from delayed rewards. A ResNet-18 with two stems trains on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 at instance-dependent noise of 40 percent, using MixMatch-style consistency for the flagged set. We test whether the policy's labels beat the pseudo-labels from co-guessing.
CONTROLS: DivideMix as the direct comparison; a pipeline where flagged samples use pseudo-labels from co-guessing; a pipeline that drops flagged samples; five seeds; paired accuracy differences.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Expect the policy's labels to add one point over co-guessing. It may fail because co-guessing already averages two networks and leaves little for exploration to improve.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Policy labels for suspected-noisy samples in complete semi-supervised pipelines on three datasets
PROPOSAL: A two-component mixture over per-sample losses flags suspected-noisy samples, which are then treated as unlabeled and relabeled by an exploring correction policy trained on delayed rewards. ResNet-18 and PreAct ResNet-34 networks learn CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet at four instance-dependent noise levels, with MixMatch-style consistency on the flagged set under three consistency weights. The question is whether policy labels outperform pseudo-labels from co-guessing.
CONTROLS: DivideMix as the direct comparison; a pipeline where flagged samples use pseudo-labels from co-guessing; a pipeline that drops flagged samples; five seeds; paired accuracy differences per cell.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Expect the policy's labels to add one point over co-guessing. It may fail because co-guessing averages two networks and leaves little for exploration to improve.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: How small can the clean reward set be? Reward signal from a tiny trusted split
PROPOSAL: A correction policy needs some reward signal. We give it a clean split of 50, 200 or 1000 labeled CIFAR-10 images, or none (agreement between two teachers only), and let it explore alternative labels under instance-dependent noise of 40 percent. A ResNet-18 trains for 100 epochs, and we report test accuracy against clean-split size, plus the correlation between reward and actual label correctness measured on the full training set.
CONTROLS: No-clean-set variant; supervised training on the tiny split only; a robust loss with no clean data; three seeds; reward-correctness correlation with bootstrap intervals.
COST: 45
PREDICTION: Expect accuracy to be flat above 200 clean images and a drop of two points with none. It may fail if the two-teacher agreement reward is already as informative as 1000 clean labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Trusted-split size and reward source study with many splits, rewards and noise levels
PROPOSAL: A correction policy needs some reward signal. We give it a clean split sized from 50 to 5000 labeled CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 images, or none, with three alternative reward sources, and let it explore alternative labels under instance-dependent noise of 20, 40 and 60 percent. A ResNet-34 trains for 200 epochs, and we report test accuracy against clean-split size, and the correlation between reward and label correctness on the training set.
CONTROLS: No-clean-set variant; supervised training on the tiny split only; a robust loss with no clean data; five seeds; reward-correctness correlation with bootstrap intervals per combination.
COST: 45
PREDICTION: Expect accuracy to be flat above 200 clean images and a drop of two points with none. It may fail if the two-teacher agreement reward is as informative as 1000 clean labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compute-matched comparison of policy-based correction with sample selection methods on WebVision
PROPOSAL: We compare the correction policy with DivideMix and ELR+ on the WebVision mini subset (100 classes, about 65000 images) at equal numbers of epochs and equal batch settings, using an Inception-ResNet-v2. Beyond accuracy, we measure wall-clock per epoch, the extra forward passes required by the policy, and how much of the gain survives when the policy's rollout is restricted to one step. We also evaluate on the 5000 ILSVRC validation images of the same classes.
CONTROLS: DivideMix and ELR+ with published settings; the policy with one-step rollouts; the policy with a shared backbone for actor and critic; five seeds with ranges; time per epoch measured on the same machine.
COST: 2500
PREDICTION: Expect the policy to match DivideMix within half a point at higher cost per epoch, with one-step rollouts keeping most of the gain. It may fail if exploration only helps at higher noise than WebVision has.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Full-scale comparison of the correction policy with selection methods on WebVision, Clothing1M and ILSVRC
PROPOSAL: We compare the correction policy with DivideMix, ELR+ and UNICON on full WebVision (1000 classes, 2400000 images), Clothing1M and ILSVRC validation at equal epochs and equal batch settings, using Inception-ResNet-v2 and ResNet-50 networks. Beyond accuracy, we measure wall-clock per epoch, the forward passes required by the policy, and how much of the gain survives when the rollout is restricted to three step counts.
CONTROLS: DivideMix, ELR+ and UNICON with published settings; the policy with one-step rollouts; the policy with a shared backbone for actor and critic; three seeds with ranges; time per epoch on identical machines.
COST: 2500
PREDICTION: Expect the policy to match DivideMix within half a point at higher cost per epoch, with one-step rollouts keeping most of the gain. It may fail if exploration only helps at higher noise than WebVision has.
